reasons: Both give two distinct one-sentence openings framed around what colleagues gain or stop suffering, and neither drifts into advice about when to send or deliver anything. B keeps every number and date as an explicit placeholder with an in-line warning not to invent it, while A's second opening states concrete figures about the new system (three days and two support threads now, half a day and none after the move) that the request never supplied, mitigated only by a trailing note to substitute real values. A is the more immediately quotable of the two and that nearly offsets the gap, but on the rubric's no-invented-facts standard B stays clean.
